modules.title: Algorithms and Data Structures
topics: Arrays, linked lists, stacks and queues
learningOutcomes: Choose an appropriate data structure for a given problem and justify the choice
Implement classic sorting and graph algorithms and analyse their running time
Reason about the correctness of an algorithm using invariants
modules.industryNote: Used in search ranking, route planning and almost every coding interview.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Programming with Java
learningOutcomes: Design small object-oriented programs from a written specification
Write readable Java code that uses the standard collections
Explain how inheritance and interfaces support reuse
modules.industryNote: Java still runs much of banking, Android and large back-end systems.

modules.title: Computer Systems and the Command Line
topics: Binary, number representation and logic gates
learningOutcomes: Explain how a program is executed by a processor
Work confidently at a Linux command line
Write and debug short C programs that manipulate memory
modules.industryNote: Most servers run Linux; comfort at the terminal pays off in every engineering job.

modules.title: Mathematics for Computer Science: Statistics and Linear Algebra
learningOutcomes: Apply probability and statistical inference to data from computing problems
Manipulate vectors and matrices and interpret them geometrically
Fit and interpret a least-squares model
modules.industryNote: The maths behind every machine learning model and A/B test you'll meet at work.

modules.title: Introduction to Programming (Python)
learningOutcomes: Write Python programs that solve well-specified problems
Use lists and dictionaries to organise data
Debug a program systematically
modules.industryNote: Python is in 62% of UK ML engineer ads and most data roles.

modules.title: First Year Team Project
topics: Working in a project team of five or six
Shared repositories on GitLab, branches and merge requests
Demonstrating a product to a client
learningOutcomes: Contribute to a shared code base using branches and merge requests
Plan work in short iterations with a team
Present a working product and reflect on the process
modules.industryNote: Branches and code review are how every software team ships, every day.

modules.title: Fundamentals of Computation
learningOutcomes: Model simple systems as finite automata
Write precise specifications in logic
Prove properties of programs by induction
modules.industryNote: Regular expressions and parsers are everyday tools in compilers, linters and data cleaning.

modules.title: Database Systems
topics: The relational model and relational algebra
learningOutcomes: Design a normalised relational schema from requirements
Express queries in relational algebra and a declarative query language
Explain how transactions keep data consistent under concurrency
modules.industryNote: Schema design is everyday work; job ads also expect fluent, hands-on SQL.

modules.title: Machine Learning
topics: Supervised learning: linear models, decision trees, k-nearest neighbours
Data preparation with pandas and NumPy
learningOutcomes: Apply supervised and unsupervised learning methods to real datasets
Evaluate a model fairly with held-out data and cross-validation
Use pandas, NumPy and scikit-learn to build a reproducible analysis
modules.industryNote: The core of every ML engineer role; 55% of UK ML engineer ads ask for it.

modules.title: Software Engineering
topics: Working with a large existing code base
learningOutcomes: Add features to a large unfamiliar code base safely
Write automated unit and integration tests
Refactor code to improve its design without changing behaviour
modules.industryNote: Testing and refactoring legacy code is most of what junior engineers do.

modules.title: Cyber Security
learningOutcomes: Identify threats to a system and propose mitigations
Explain how cryptographic primitives protect data
Find and fix common web vulnerabilities
modules.industryNote: Secure-by-default habits are expected in every engineering team.

modules.title: Operating Systems
learningOutcomes: Explain how an operating system shares the processor and memory
Write concurrent C programs that avoid race conditions
Compare scheduling and memory management strategies
modules.industryNote: Concurrency and memory bugs are what separate good back-end engineers.

modules.title: Deep Learning
topics: Optimisation and regularisation for deep networks
learningOutcomes: Derive and implement backpropagation from first principles
Design convolutional networks for image classification
Diagnose training problems such as vanishing gradients
modules.industryNote: Behind computer vision and speech products; industry builds these in a framework like PyTorch.

modules.title: Distributed Systems
learningOutcomes: Explain the trade-offs between consistency, availability and partition tolerance
Design a fault-tolerant service from requirements
Analyse how a system behaves under failure
modules.industryNote: The theory behind system design interviews and every large web service.

modules.title: Natural Language Processing
learningOutcomes: Explain how modern neural models represent text
Build a text classifier and analyse its errors
Discuss the limitations and biases of language technologies
modules.industryNote: The theory under chat assistants; building and testing LLM apps isn't covered here.

modules.title: Third Year Project
topics: Choosing and scoping an individual project
Writing a dissertation and giving a demonstration
learningOutcomes: Plan and deliver a substantial individual software project
Test and critically evaluate your own work
Write a clear technical report and present it
modules.industryNote: A finished project you can explain is the strongest thing on a graduate CV.
